newsitem.title: USA: CHINA RUMORS SWAY U.S. SOY EXPORT TRADE ESTIMATES.
newsitem.headline: CHINA RUMORS SWAY U.S. SOY EXPORT TRADE ESTIMATES.

text.p: Trade estimates for U.S. new crop soybean exports varied widely on Wednesday amid rumors that China may have cancelled new crop U.S. soybean purchases.

"There is some talk that there might be some new crop cancellations," one analyst said. "The rumor I was hearing was that it may be up to 400,000 (tonnes) cancelled so there could actually be a negative number out there."

The U.S. Agriculture Department will release its weekly export sales data at 0730 CDT/1230 GMT Thursday. Trade sources expected the report to show new crop soybean sales at anywhere from minus 300,000 tonnes to plus 300,000 tonnes.
Rumors have swirled at the Chicago Board of Trade that China cancelled new and old crop soybean purchases but U.S. export sources were unable to confirm any cancellations.
"I think (the cancellations) have been factored into the market but a negative number on tomorrow's report could catch some people by surprise," an oilseeds analyst said.
